name: xcodes (aria2 downloads)
baseline: Single-connection URLSession download of Xcode (xcodes without aria2, or a browser download)
verdict_reason: With aria2 installed, xcodes downloads Xcode over up to 16 connections and claims 3-5x faster than URLSession. The claim is first-party and unmeasured in public, but the mechanism is straightforward; the gain depends on the network and per-connection limits.
tier_reason: First-party README claim with no timings, network or method.
claimed_speedup: Downloads Xcode 3-5x faster than URLSession using up to 16 connections
workload: Downloading Xcode .xip archives from Apple's servers
install: Homebrew (brew install xcodesorg/made/xcodes), plus brew install aria2
one_liner: Command-line Xcode installer that downloads over up to 16 connections with aria2, claimed 3-5x faster than URLSession.
how_it_is_fast: When aria2 is on the PATH, xcodes hands the download to it, which splits the file into ranges fetched over up to 16 parallel connections, getting around per-connection throughput limits. It can then extract with unxip instead of xip.
use_it_when: Installing or switching Xcode versions on CI machines or several developer Macs
Networks where a single HTTP connection does not saturate the link
skip_it_when: Networks or proxies that throttle per client rather than per connection
Environments that disallow third-party download tools or Apple ID logins from scripts
caveats: No published measurement; 3-5x depends on network and server limits
The speedup comes from aria2, a separate C++ download tool, not from xcodes' Swift code
tradeoffs: Requires Apple ID authentication for downloads

evidence.quote: It uses up to 16 connections to download Xcode 3-5x faster than URLSession.
